D011-D012_h001.question:
"Lately, I've just been… on edge, you know? It’s not a constant, overarching dread about everything, but there's this specific thing that just paralyses me. If I see open spaces – a giant empty parking lot, a wide-open field, even a particularly spacious film set – my heart just starts pounding. It's ridiculous, I know, but I can feel this intense fear grip me. My muscles just lock up; my neck and shoulders feel like they’re made of concrete, and it's practically impossible to relax until I'm out of that situation.

It’s been going on for over seven months now. These worries about encountering an open space will just intrude on my thoughts, even when I'm trying to focus on cutting a scene. I'll be in the editing suite, completely immersed, and then BAM – a thought of being in an empty park just floods my mind, and I can't concentrate. It's frustrating because in every other aspect of my life – my work, my finances, my relationships – I'm completely fine. It's only when faced with these wide-open areas that I completely unravel."
D011-D012_h001.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h002.question: "Lately, I've just been a bundle of nerves, Doc. It's mostly revolved around my job at the factory. We handle some pretty heavy machinery, and the thought of something going wrong, especially with the crane, just paralyzes me. I keep picturing the cables snapping, or a load dropping on someone. It’s like one worry about the crane just chains to another, and before I know it, I’m imagining the whole place falling apart. I can’t relax, even at home; my shoulders and neck feel like concrete. The slightest unexpected noise, like a door slamming, makes me jump out of my skin. This constant worrying about the crane has been going on for over seven months now. It's the only thing that really gets me worked up like this. Outside of anything related to the crane or heavy machinery, I don’t really get this anxious about much else."
D011-D012_h002.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h003.question: "Lately, I've just been… on edge, you know? It’s not a constant thing but when it hits, the worry just intrudes out of nowhere. I’ll be up on a roof, trying to focus on an installation, and suddenly my mind is racing with 'what if' scenarios. Not about my job, or my marriage, or anything broad like that. It's always about the dogs. I can practically feel my muscles clenching up, especially in my neck and shoulders, and I can't shake that stiff, tense feeling. It’s like my whole body just locks up. This has been going on for the better part of a year now. I just can't seem to relax thinking about them."
D011-D012_h003.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h004.question: "Lately, it's like I'm always on edge. Every little sound at home, even my wife moving around, makes me jump. My neck and shoulders are constantly throbbing, like I've been in a wrestling match. It's not just physical; my mind is racing. If something minor goes wrong with a case, I immediately jump to the worst-case scenario – that I'll miss something crucial, a criminal will get away, and innocent people will suffer. These worries just pop into my head, completely derailing my focus when I'm trying to review files. But the strange thing is, all this intense fear and anxiety… it really only happens when I'm dealing with these crime scene photos and autopsy reports. When I'm off duty, or even on other parts of a case not involving those specific, graphic images, I don't feel this overwhelming dread. It's solely tied to them."
D011-D012_h004.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h005.question:
Lately, it’s been hell, doc. I’m 35, married, and my plumbing business is my life, but I can't even get through a job without my stomach churning. What really gets me is the heights. Any time a job means getting up on a ladder, or even a tall roof, my mind just goes blank with this awful dread. I start thinking the worst — that the ladder will collapse, or I’ll slip and break my neck, and then what? My wife, the business… it all comes crashing down.

That fear, it just pops into my head out of nowhere, even when I'm just looking at a tall building from the ground. I'll be in the middle of fixing a leaky pipe, my hands working fine, and then suddenly this picture of me falling flashes, and I can't concentrate on anything else. My whole body tenses up, especially my neck and shoulders; they get so stiff I can barely turn my head. It's like I'm wound up so tight that I just can't sit still, my leg constantly bouncing. But it’s only when I'm dealing with heights, or even thinking about them; other than that, I feel completely normal. It’s been going on for a few months now, and it’s really starting to mess with my work.
D011-D012_h005.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h006.question:
It's taken a lot for me to come here, honestly. I've always been a bit on edge, but this past year, it’s really ramped up. The worry is just… everywhere. It's not just my voice acting gigs, though I stress about whether I'll get enough work, if my performance will be good enough, or if the next job will come. It bleeds into everything. I worry about my parents' health, even though they're fine. I worry about my finances, even when I'm doing well. I worry about just… everything, really.

And sleeping? Forget about it. I can be in bed for eight hours, but I wake up feeling like I've run a marathon. I'm so tense, like my nerves are buzzing, and the smallest sound will make me jump out of my skin. A car door slamming outside, a notification on my phone – it just throws me. It feels like I can’t relax, ever. This constant state of unease has been with me for as long as I can remember, and honestly, I just want some relief.
D011-D012_h006.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h007.question: "Lately, I just feel… on edge, you know? Like my nerves are constantly frayed. The smallest sound, like my roommate dropping a pen, sends a jolt through me. It's not like this all the time, though. It really kicks in when I have to think about or actually do presentations. My stomach drops, my heart races… I actually missed a graduate seminar last week because I just couldn't make myself go into that lecture hall. I spent the whole night before wide awake, just dreading it, even though I know it's a ridiculous fear. I keep thinking, 'what if I stutter, what if I forget everything, what if everyone laughs?' I spiral into thinking I'll fail out of my program over one bad presentation. Then, the next day, I just crashed – slept nearly twelve hours, wishing I could disappear. Honestly, outside of anything related to public speaking, I feel fine. My studies are on track, and my personal life is okay, but this one thing just devastates me."
D011-D012_h007.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h008.question: "Well, doctor, it's mostly the elevators. I know it sounds silly for an 82-year-old, but the thought of getting in one just paralyzes me. I keep picturing it getting stuck, or worse, plummeting, and I just can't shake it. This fear has really taken over. I find myself waking up around 4 AM most mornings, heart pounding, all wound up and keyed up just thinking about the possibility of having to ride one. I try to avoid them at all costs, even if it means struggling up several flights of stairs. It’s not like I’m generally a worrier; I don’t fret about my health, or my family, or anything else really. It’s just this one thing, this intense fear, that stops me in my tracks."
D011-D012_h008.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h009.question:
"Lately, I've just been a mess. It's not like I'm worried about every little thing, my work at the plant is fine, and my finances are stable. It's really just focused on flying. My sister is getting married overseas next month, and the thought of getting on that plane is just unbearable. I keep asking myself, 'What if there's turbulence? What if the engine fails?' These 'what ifs' just go on and on, and I can't shake them.

It's gotten so bad that I’m waking up at 3 AM most nights, heart pounding, and my mind immediately goes to the flight. Then I can’t get back to sleep. During the day, I’m constantly on edge. A car horn honking or a sudden noise in the office makes me jump out of my skin. This feeling of dread and unease is really only tied to this damn trip. If it weren't for having to fly, I honestly think everything else would be fine."
D011-D012_h009.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h010.question: It all started about eight months ago, not long after that warehouse fire. Lately, I've been waking up around 3 AM, heart pounding, and my body feels like a coiled spring – just completely stiff. No matter how much I try, I can't fall back asleep. It's only when I'm dealing with fires or enclosed, smoky spaces that I feel this way. The thought of being trapped, the heat, the smoke... sometimes I get this awful fear that one small spark could lead to an irreversible explosion, or that we'll be totally engulfed with no way out. But outside of that? I'm fine. At home with my wife, even on the job when we're not on a call, I’m my usual self. It's just that one thing, the fires themselves, that fills me with dread.
D011-D012_h010.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h011.question: "Lately, I just can't seem to get a proper night's sleep. The dreams are so vivid and unsettling, always about *it*, leaving me feeling drained the moment I wake up. Even simple things at my data entry job, like typing, feel like a monumental effort; my body just aches with exhaustion. It's frustrating because I *try* to push the thoughts away, I really do, but it's like a broken record in my head. This constant worry, this dread, it’s always about one thing though – whenever I think about being in a small, enclosed space. It's not like I'm anxious about work, or my marriage, or anything else; it's just this one specific fear that consumes me."
D011-D012_h011.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h012.question:
Lately doc, I haven't been myself. It’s been about seven months now. When I try to sleep, I'm plagued by these wrenching nightmares; they're all about the plane crashing, feeling that sickening drop, and the screams. I wake up in a cold sweat, heart pounding. Even when I do get some rest, I just feel drained. Getting through my pre-flight checks, even just small tasks at home, feels like a monumental effort. My wife says I'm withdrawn.

The worst part is, I try to push these thoughts away. I tell myself it's irrational, that I'm a professional, but I just can't shake it. It’s this constant, gnawing dread specifically when I’m getting ready for a flight, or even just thinking about being in the cockpit. It doesn't really pop up in other parts of my life – not with my marriage, my finances, or even general health. It's really just centered on this flying business. I used to love it, you know? Now, the thought of stepping onto that flight deck just fills me with terror.
D011-D012_h012.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h013.question: "Lately, sleep has been a struggle. I wake up feeling like I haven't slept a wink, even if I’ve been in bed for hours. My body just feels so heavy, tired all the time, even simple things like walking to the mailbox wear me out. It's like a constant dread, especially when I think about the geese at the pond. One thought leads to another – if I go to the park, what if they chase me? What if I trip? What if I fall and can’t get up? It seems silly, I know, but this overwhelming fear just takes over when I imagine encountering them. I recognize it's probably excessive, but this intense fear and anxiety are really only tied to specific situations involving geese. Otherwise, I’m generally quite calm and don't really worry much about anything else in my life."
D011-D012_h013.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h014.question:
It's been a few months now, and I just can't shake this feeling. Every night, it’s a battle to fall asleep. My mind just races, replaying the images from that one incident. I’ll lie there for what feels like hours, just staring at the ceiling. And then, even if I get some sleep, I wake up utterly exhausted, like I haven't rested at all. This fatigue has been constant, making it so hard to focus on anything.

Out on a case, or even at home with my wife, these worries just pop into my head. It’s always about the unexpected, the sudden lunge, the bite. It’s ridiculous, I know, especially for a detective. I can handle dangerous situations, but now the thought of dogs... it consumes me. It interferes with everything. I'm not worried about my job, or my marriage, or money – it's just this one thing, this intense fear, that I can't get past. Nothing else seems to trigger this kind of anxiety, just them.
D011-D012_h014.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h015.question: It's been six months now, and I just can't shake this feeling. I’m utterly exhausted, even after a pretty good night’s rest. I wake up constantly, usually around 2 or 3 AM, and then my mind just starts racing. It’s always about the markets, specifically the volatility. I'll worry about one stock, then it'll snowball into how that affects the whole portfolio, then my clients, then my career, and before I know it, I’m picturing myself losing everything. It’s a vicious cycle. The worst part is this intense fear that wells up when I think about the impending market crash – it’s a specific, overwhelming dread that cripples me when I’m at work or even just watching the news. My wife says I'm always on edge, but honestly, it’s only when I'm dealing with or even just thinking about the stock market. Other than that, everything else feels pretty normal.
D011-D012_h015.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D012_h016.question: Lately, I’ve just felt… drained. Getting out of bed feels like a monumental task, and the energy I used to have for job hunting or even just talking to people is completely gone. My mind often goes blank; it's like a sudden white noise, and I can't even focus on simple things. I'm constantly caught in ‘what if’ scenarios, especially about finding a job, but it's not really about everything in my life. It's really just when I think about going into crowded places, like job fairs or a busy interview waiting room. The thought of all those people, it just paralyses me with fear. Otherwise, I’m generally okay – it's really contained to those public situations.
D011-D012_h016.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D011-D012_h017.question: "Lately, I just can't shake this feeling of being on edge. It's not like I'm worried about everything, not really. It’s more… focused. It started a few months ago, maybe four or five. I try to prepare for my presentations, but my mind just keeps jumping all over the place. I can't seem to hold onto a thought, especially when I know a certain client is going to be there. I'm constantly asking 'what if' about how things are going to go specifically with them. I'm completely drained, too. I get plenty of sleep, but I wake up feeling like I’ve run a marathon. It’s strange because outside of dealing with *those* particular client meetings, I feel more or less fine. My personal life, other projects, even dating – none of that really triggers this kind of intense dread or makes me feel this exhausted or scatterbrained. It's really just those specific situations that throw me off. I can't keep living like this."
D011-D012_h017.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D011-D012_h018.question: It all started a few months ago, right after I moved into the dorms. I just feel constantly on edge, but it’s not just about academics or fitting in. It’s when I think about going into the communal showers, or even just seeing pictures of them online. My mind immediately flashes to the worst possible scenario – I'll slip, hit my head, and nobody will find me for hours. I know it sounds ridiculous, but just thinking about it makes me so tired. Like, draining tired, to the point where even getting out of bed feels monumental. And then, when I try to study, my thoughts just scatter. It’s like a constant hum of dread in the back of my mind, always circling back to those showers. I can't concentrate on my lectures or readings; my attention just fragments. It's not like I'm worried about exams or my roommates, it’s just this one thing, but it’s really messing me up.
D011-D012_h018.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D011-D012_h019.question:
"It’s just…everything feels so heavy lately. I'm always tired, like my body wants to shut down even after doing nothing all day. And my mind, sometimes it just goes completely blank. I'll be sitting in class, trying to listen, and suddenly it's just… nothing. No thoughts, no understanding, just a void.

The worst part is, it's really starting to affect my studies, especially when it comes to presentations or even just speaking up in class. The thought of it… my heart starts pounding, my palms get sweaty, and I can't breathe. It’s like all those 'what ifs' just flood in – 'What if I mess up? What if everyone laughs?' I get stuck in those thoughts and can't move past them.

This feeling, this constant dread, only really happens when I know I have to speak in front of people, or even just be the center of attention. When I'm just hanging out with my friends or doing my own thing, I feel totally fine. But as soon as that specific situation comes up, I'm a complete mess."
D011-D012_h019.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D011-D012_h020.question: "It's been a tough six months, doc. Ever since I lost my last job, it feels like I'm constantly on edge. I mean, it's not like I'm worried about *everything* all the time. It’s mostly when I think about going into a job interview. My heart starts pounding, my palms get sweaty, and I feel this intense dread. The thought of walking into that room, meeting new people, having them judge me… it just paralyzes me. I try to prepare, to focus on what I need to say, but my mind just races. I can't concentrate on anything for more than a few minutes. I'm so drained all the time, completely exhausted, even if I haven't really done anything. It's like my body is heavy and I just want to lie down. It's really just the interview situations that get to me; otherwise, I feel pretty okay."
D011-D012_h020.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D011-D012_h021.question: It's like I'm constantly on edge, but not about everything. I worry quite a bit about my kids and my work performance, but I can usually manage to put those thoughts aside eventually. The real issue is when I see a spider. My mind just goes completely blank. It’s like all the thoughts in my head just drain away, replaced by pure terror. It’s not just a little unease; it's an intense, overwhelming fear that washes over me. I try to tell myself it's just a small bug, but I absolutely cannot control the panic. This has been happening for as long as I can remember, and it’s genuinely debilitating. The anxiety is really just focused on those specific situations, like finding a spider in the house or even seeing a picture of one. Other things in my life, while sometimes stressful, don't trigger this same crippling level of fear.

A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D011-D012_h022.question: Lately, everything just feels… overwhelming. It’s not just one thing, you know? D011-D012_h023.question: I'm really struggling, doc. It's not just one thing, you know? My mind is constantly buzzing, and it feels like everything is a potential catastrophe. D011-D012_h024.question:
"Lately, it feels like my world has shrunk. I can't shake this feeling of dread, especially when I think about going into a classroom with a fire alarm. It’s not just a fleeting thought; it’s a constant, 'what if' loop that really gets going whenever I even *imagine* a fire alarm going off. One thought leads to another, like, 'What if it goes off during class?' then 'What if I can't get everyone out in time?' then 'What if someone gets hurt?' It just spirals into this catastrophic scenario.

And it’s only with this. It’s weird, because once I know there’s no fire alarm around, or if I’m not in a school setting, I’m actually fine. I can enjoy a movie, go for a run, even grade papers without a problem. But the moment that specific situation comes to mind, the anxiety hits hard. I find myself unable to sustain attention, my mind entirely consumed by these scenarios. It's really affecting my ability to teach effectively. I dread the bell ringing, not because of the students, but because I’m so focused on my escape route, the nearest exit, and where my students are."
D011-D012_h024.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D011-D012_h025.question: It's getting harder to just... function normally. I'm 47 and a bankruptcy lawyer, so I'm used to high-stress situations, but this is different. I'll be in the middle of drafting a motion, and suddenly my mind is racing about the subway, and I can't concentrate on the legal documents in front of me for the life of me. My focus is just shattered. I try to push it out of my head, but it keeps coming back. It’s only ever about the subway, though. Outside of that, I’m completely fine.
